best_for: Windows PC builders, overclockers and IT staff who want a detailed sensor readout, and who will pay once HWiNFO runs on a work machine.

points.title: Free means personal use
points.text: The free build is for personal, non-commercial use. On a work machine it is allowed only for a 14-day evaluation; after that it needs a Pro license.

points.title: Not every Pro license covers work
points.text: Pro comes as Personal, Engineer or Corporate. Personal (1 user, 5 computers) is still not for commercial use. Engineer is licensed per user and Corporate per computer, and only those two cover work.

points.title: Shared Memory stops after 12 hours
points.text: Overlays and remote monitoring read HWiNFO's sensors through Shared Memory. In the free build it switches off after 12 hours of running and has to be turned back on by hand. Pro removes the limit, and also lifts the 5-item cap on the on-screen display.

points.title: Pro is cheap to start, renewals optional
points.text: A subscription starts at USD 29 for the first year and USD 14.50 to renew, and a lifetime license at USD 199. Versions released during your maintenance period keep working after it ends. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Windows 7 and later, 64-bit
points.text: HWiNFO64 needs 64-bit Windows 7 or later. A 32-bit build and a DOS build also exist, but the 32-bit one supports fewer cores and less memory on 64-bit systems.

points.title: x64 and Arm64 installers here
points.text: This page lists x64 and Arm64 installers. Both install machine-wide, so they need administrator rights. The Windows listing keeps 4 versions, so older releases need another source.
